narrative.headline: Drive Slack from the terminal as yourself using your browser session, across all your separate-login workspaces, with offline sync and native Slack AI.
narrative.value_prop: Authenticates with your own xoxc session token plus the d cookie, so there's no app to create and no admin approval. Every workspace you're logged into becomes a named account with its own local SQLite mirror, so you can search, catch up, and run cross-workspace digests offline. Includes ai ask, which routes through Slack's own AI assistant.
narrative.auth_narrative: Uses your logged-in browser session: the xoxc token (Authorization) plus the d cookie. Provide them per account via env vars (SLACK_XOXC_TOKEN, SLACK_D_COOKIE) or `auth login`. The d cookie can be exchanged for a fresh xoxc automatically. Session tokens rotate and can be invalidated by Slack on bursty access, so the CLI syncs to a local mirror and paginates conservatively; run `doctor` to check validity per account.

quickstart.comment: list channels and DMs in the active account

troubleshoots.fix: Your xoxc/d session was invalidated; re-grab the d cookie and run `auth login`, or run `doctor`.
Slow down: rely on `sync` + offline queries instead of repeated live calls; respect Retry-After.

narrative.when_to_use: Use when you want to read, search, send, and catch up on Slack as yourself from the terminal or an agent, especially across multiple separate-login workspaces, without creating a Slack app. Strong for offline/cheap repeated queries via the local mirror and for cross-workspace digests.
anti_triggers: Building a shared bot or integration for a team (use an official Slack app + bot token instead)
Anything requiring OAuth scopes you'd grant to a third party
